q: You read a CSV folder with `option("header", "true")` but no schema and no `inferSchema`. What type do the columns get?
o: The types stored in the CSV header
STRING for every column
Whatever types the target table has
INT for numbers, STRING for the rest
e: CSV carries no type information. Without a schema or inference, Spark reads every column as a string.

q: Why is an explicit schema usually better than `inferSchema` in a production job?
o: Inference is not supported on serverless
Inference only works on JSON files
Explicit schemas compress the data better
Inference costs an extra pass over the data and the types can change between runs
e: To infer types Spark must scan the files before the real read, and new files with odd values can change the inferred types.

q: A nightly job runs `df.write.mode("append").saveAsTable("sales")`. It fails half-way, and you simply re-run it. What is the risk?
o: Rows that were already appended by a successful earlier run of the same data are added again
The table is dropped
The schema is inferred again
Nothing: append is always safe to repeat
e: Append adds whatever the DataFrame holds. Re-running the same input appends the same rows a second time unless you overwrite or merge.

o: Copies the data into a new Delta table
Writes the DataFrame to a volume
Gives the DataFrame's plan a name that SQL in the same session can query
Caches the DataFrame in memory
e: A temp view is only a name for a plan, valid in the current session. SQL and DataFrames share the same engine, so `spark.sql` can query it.

q: Which write makes the result a table in Unity Catalog that others can query by name?
o: `df.write.format("parquet").save("/Volumes/c/s/v/out")`
`df.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable("sales_clean")`
`df.show()`
`df.createOrReplaceTempView("sales_clean")`
e: `saveAsTable` registers a managed (Delta by default) table in the current catalog and schema. `save(path)` writes only files, and a temp view disappears with the session.
